messages:
maria: heads-up — I enabled the small-inline-prefetch path in the fused-attn scheduler on staging and we saw a ~12% tail-latency regression on long sequences :thinking:
ajit: ugh, when you say long sequences what's the length distribution?
sam: any chance it’s due to lane starvation on the fused kernel when batch shapes vary? last time we saw that with mixed seqs
maria: 1) seqs 1024/1536/2048, 2) batching heuristic kept bundling small+large in same batch to hit throughput, 3) perf-bot traces attached below
perf-bot: summary: mean latency up 4%, p99 up 12%, kernel-level hotspot: fused_attn_prefetch_inline (kernel id: fa_pref_03) showing warp-occupancy dip on SMs 4-7
jin: can you paste the microprofile snippet? also which nvprof counters looked weird
maria: here are the relevant snippets:
```
# from nvprof sample
Kernel: fa_pref_03  Time: 1.23ms  AchievedOccupancy: 0.48  L2_read_throughput: 12GB/s  L1_hit_rate: 0.35
Kernel: fa_normal   Time: 0.98ms  AchievedOccupancy: 0.74  L2_read_throughput: 18GB/s  L1_hit_rate: 0.62
```
ajit: L1 hit rate drop is telling. inline prefetch probably evicts useful epilogue buffers for some lanes, causing cache thrash
sam: that + mixed sequence lengths can cause some warps to idle waiting for slow lanes while others run ahead — effective occupancy suffers
maria: i also grabbed a callgraph from our tracer (shortened):
```
serve_loop -> schedule_batch -> fused_attn_call -> prefetch_inline -> epilogue_fuse -> write_kv_cache
```
so prefetch_inline is before epilogue_fuse in the fast path
jin: interesting — if prefetch touches the same address space as epilogue fusing writes, we could be contending on L2/L1 bandwidth. Suggest moving prefetch after epilogue writes or switching to non-temporal loads for prefetch
ajit: another angle: our batcher is bundling heterogeneous seq-length requests into the same dispatch to increase token throughput, but fused kernel is sensitive to shape uniformity. Maybe the heuristic needs a penalty term for fused_attn_prefetch path
maria: agreed. I ran a quick A/B: disabling inline-prefetch for fused_attn on mixed-shape batches restores baseline (p99 back within 1-2%)
sam: can we add a cheap probe in scheduler: if batch has >X% seq variance, route to conservative kernel (no-inline-prefetch)
jin: also add a runtime metric: track warp-idle-time per kernel and expose in console. That will make future regressions visible without digging into nvprof
ajit: for long-term root cause we should repro with microbench harness: create a mixed-shape batch rig that mimics production arrival order and run kernels under nvprof + nsight to capture bank conflicts and memory pressure
maria: filed a small task: PERF-1387 to add the batching penalty + runtime warp idle metric. Added logs from the A/B here:
```
A: fused_prefetch_on mixed batch p99=14.2ms
B: fused_prefetch_off mixed batch p99=12.8ms
Baseline (uniform large seq): p99=11.5ms
```
sam: thanks — one more thought: KV cache behavior — does prefetch read/write the same page granularity that our paged-kv uses? If prefetch touches entire pages it could be forcing page migration/eviction and causing extra latency for subsequent reads
maria: good catch — our paged-kv uses 64KB pages; inline-prefetch currently does coarse 256KB prefetch to amortize overhead. that's probably too big
ajit: make it configurable per kernel: prefetch granularity should align with paged-kv page size or be a fraction of it
jin: and instrument cache miss amplification in paged-kv when prefetched ranges overlap with writebacks
maria: action items summarized: 1) roll back inline-prefetch default for mixed-shape batches (temporary) 2) add batching variance penalty in scheduler 3) make prefetch granularity kernel-configurable and align with paged-kv 4) add warp-idle telemetry in console 5) repro harness for mixed-shape microbenching (nvprof/nsight)
sam: do we want a quick canary push to staging with rollback flag so we can A/B at scale?
maria: yes — I'll push a canary and flip off inline-prefetch for batches with seq-variance > 20%. monitor perf-bot
perf-bot: canary deployed to staging cluster-3 at 2348811200; monitoring p99/warp-idle/kv-miss-amplification
ajit: thanks team. tagging perf and runtime to keep eyes: @eng-runtime @eng-sre :eyes:
maria: and I'll open a follow-up thread with microbench results once repro is nailed down. thx everyone :thumbsup:
